data.name: Bhupat
data.gender_notes: Bhupat is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Bhupat is a Sanskrit name derived from the roots 'bhu' meaning earth and 'pat' meaning master or ruler. The name signifies the one who rules over the earth. In Hindu mythology, Bhupat is a title of various gods and goddesses, including Lord Vishnu, Lord Shiva, and Goddess Durga. The name Bhupat carries the meaning “Lord of the earth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bhupat usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the earth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine ruler of the earth, embodying the qualities of stability, protection, and nurturing.
data.etymology: Bhupat belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the earth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bhupat total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: Bhupat is a significant name in Indian culture, representing power, authority, and sovereignty over the earth. It holds a special place in Hindu mythology, where various deities are revered as Bhupat or Bhagvan Bhupati, meaning the Lord of the Earth. The name reflects a deep connection with the land and the belief in the divine presence of the deity as the supreme ruler.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Bhupat signifies the inner ruler or the Jagat-pat, the master of the world. It represents the awakened consciousness that rules over the external world, providing stability, security, and peace within. The name encourages one to connect with their inner divinity, tune into their spiritual side, and strive for self-mastery and inner growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bhupat: Lord of the Earth. Signifies one who holds the power and responsibility over the material world, nurturing and protecting it with wisdom and love.
